l1_words.meaning: to carry out or to accomplish
to take on (a role or responsibility)

pattern_explanation: The Portuguese words and their English look-alikes share a Latin root and a similar spelling, so learners may assume the English word has the same meaning. The English word has a different meaning, so the learner has to map each Portuguese word to its true English equivalent, such as a volunteer taking on a role in a youth programme.
false_friend_warning: Warning: the Portuguese verb 'assistir' means to watch or to attend, not to help, while the English verb 'assist' means to help. Also, the Portuguese word 'atual' means current, but the English word 'actual' means real or existing.
